topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by welcoming students and setting out the lecture's core objectives regarding cancer treatment approaches and mechanisms.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities that physically remove tumors or kill dividing cells, detailing their mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and drug resistance via efflux pumps.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapies that exploit intrinsic biological weaknesses in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, defective cell cycle checkpoints, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Inhibiting oncogenic kinases and overcoming resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address targeted small-molecule therapies directed against hyperactivated oncogenic kinases, detailing their molecular mechanisms, structural vulnerabilities, and pathways of acquired resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeted therapeutics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic antibodies directed at cell-surface antigens to inhibit oncogenic signaling, engage cytotoxic effector mechanisms, or selectively deliver toxic chemical payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune system engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore cancer immunotherapy approaches that harness, reactivate, or genetically engineer the adaptive immune system to recognize and eradicate tumor cells.

topics.label: Current challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of cancer therapy by reviewing systemic clinical hurdles, historical gains in survival, future treatment avenues, and ethical dilemmas.
